name: Second Acts: Revivals and Comebacks
description: Languages spoken again, bridges rebuilt, nations restored and old learning reborn: places, tongues and traditions that came back after being lost or broken.

checkpoints.name: Echoes of antiquity
checkpoints.note: The Ancient Olympic Games end in the 390s, and the Carolingian Renaissance under Charlemagne copies old books and revives learning in the ninth century.

checkpoints.name: Learning reborn
checkpoints.note: Neo-Confucianism renews an old teaching in China, and the Renaissance and Renaissance humanism bring back the learning of Greece and Rome in Europe.

checkpoints.name: Revival as style and nation
checkpoints.note: Gothic Revival architecture and Neoclassicism bring old forms back into fashion. The Partitions of Poland erase a country, and the Meiji Restoration renews Japan. Hebrew is revived as a spoken language, the Zionist movement forms, and the Olympic Games return in Athens in 1896.

checkpoints.name: Countries and languages return
checkpoints.note: Poland returns to the map in 1918, and Israel is founded in 1948. The Manx language loses its last native speaker in 1974 but is brought back by learners, and the Maori language is revived through schools from the 1980s.

checkpoints.name: The comeback age
checkpoints.note: Germany is reunified and Lithuania regains independence in 1990, Stari Most is rebuilt in Mostar in 2004, and Notre-Dame de Paris reopens after its fire in 2019.
